verdict.rationale: Attio documents a public REST API that reads and writes workspace data. It documents rate-limit responses (429 with Retry-After) and offers signed webhooks that push real-time change events, covering bidirectional sync, rate limits and change detection. Nothing in the evidence shows an upsert endpoint or any bulk or high-volume sync capability. missing for 10: documented upsert/assert-by-matching-attribute endpoint, bulk/batch or at-scale sync guidance (specific rate-limit quotas, pagination for large syncs), independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can sync records bidirectionally through the API at scale, with documented rate limits, upserts, and change detection

citations.quote: This allows developers to build apps that read and write information to and from Attio workspaces. You can also subscribe to events in realtime using webhooks.
Rate limit responses always have the HTTP status code `429`. They also always include a `Retry-After` header
Webhooks allow you to subscribe to changes that happen in Attio and then receive real-time HTTP requests to a chosen target URL to notify you of these changes.
Attio provides a public REST API which exchanges JSON over HTTPS.
